what: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: modelterms lightweight, zero-dependency R package providing unified interface manipulating stats::terms objects, formulas, fitted models, character vectors term labels. designed standalone utility statistical modeling workflows helper module packages (including future versions midr).

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: R, model terms serve structural blueprint predictive model, role paramount importance additive models built stats::lm(), stats::glm(), GAMs. However, term “terms” historically suffered ambiguity. instance, appears terms argument stats::predict.lm() accepts character vectors additive components, whereas "terms" objects stored inside fitted models formula packed complex attributes, character vectors, interchangeable. Furthermore, Base R’s stats::terms() stats::drop.terms() provide powerful formula parsing, working programmatically often involves sharp edges: Inconsistent Coercion: stats::terms() directly coerce character vector term labels like c("x1", "x2"), stats::reformulate(character(0)) throws error. Unwanted Reordering & Renaming: Even keep.order = TRUE, stats::terms() silently rewrites interaction labels based variable appearance order (e.g., turning c("", "b:") c("", ":b")). Fragile Subsetting: stats::drop.terms() requires numeric indices, loses response variable default, crashes terms dropped. Ambiguous “Variables”: Base R lacks unified way distinguish term labels (term names additive models, e.g., "x1:log(x2)"), model variables (transformed variable names formula, e.g., "log(x2)"), underlying raw variables (column names data.frame, e.g., "x2"). modelterms resolves issues clean, pipe-friendly functional API.

what: 1. Flexible and Safe Coercion with as_terms()
title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: as_terms() accepts terms objects, formulas, fitted models (lm, glm, etc.), character vectors. Strict Term Label Vectors (length >= 2): Every element must valid single term. Input order exact interaction notation ("b:") strictly preserved. Formula Shorthand (length == 1): single string containing formula operators (e.g., ".^2" "* b + c") expanded formula right-hand side.
code: library(modelterms)  # Preserves exact order and "b:a" notation for term label vectors t1 <- as_terms(c("b:a", "a", "1")) get_labels(t1) #> [1] "b:a" "a" has_intercept(t1) #> [1] TRUE  # Expands length-1 formula shorthands (including "." with data) t2 <- as_terms(".^2", y = "Ozone", data = airquality[, 1:4]) get_labels(t2) #> [1] "Solar.R"      "Wind"         "Temp"         "Solar.R:Wind" "Solar.R:Temp" #> [6] "Wind:Temp"

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: filter_terms() subsets “terms” object interaction order, required variables, excluded variables. Unlike stats::drop.terms(), safely returns intercept-(empty) “terms” object even terms filtered .
code: fml <- log(Ozone) ~ Solar.R + Wind + Temp + Wind:Temp + Solar.R:Wind  # Extract main effects only as a character vector fml |> filter_terms(order = 1) |> get_labels() #> [1] "Solar.R" "Wind"    "Temp"  # Keep terms involving "Wind", but exclude any term involving "Solar.R" sub_terms <- filter_terms(fml, require = "Wind", remove = "Solar.R") get_labels(sub_terms) #> [1] "Wind"      "Wind:Temp"  # Directly use the filtered terms object to fit a submodel lm_sub <- lm(sub_terms, data = airquality)

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms
text: users specify interaction terms plotting evaluation functions, may write "Temp:Wind" instead "Wind:Temp". match_labels() normalizes matches terms regardless variable order rejecting multi-term expressions like "Wind * Temp".
code: labs <- c("x1", "log(x2)", "x1:log(x2)", "I(1:100):x1")  # Matches reversed interaction notation to the canonical model labels match_labels(c("log(x2):x1", "x1:I(1:100)", "x1"), labs) #> [1] "x1:log(x2)"  "I(1:100):x1" "x1"  # Safely handles unmatched or invalid expressions ("pass", "omit", or "fail") match_labels(c("x1", "x1 * x2", "unknown"), labs, nomatch = "omit") #> [1] "x1"

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels — modelterms
text: x, y object representing model terms: terms object, formula, fitted model object, character vector. as_terms(), y specifies optional response variable (character string language object). match_labels(), y target object whose term labels matched . intercept logical. as_terms(), intercept included default coercing character vector? Defaults FALSE. Explicit tokens x ("1" "+1") override default. filter_terms(), whether retain intercept x. data data.frame used resolve . formulas shorthand strings. keep.order logical. terms kept input order rather sorted interaction order? Defaults TRUE strict term label vectors FALSE formulas length-1 formula shorthands. env environment attach resulting terms object coercing character vector. Defaults parent.frame(). ... additional arguments passed terms as_terms(). raw logical. FALSE (default get_variables() get_response()), returns model expressions (e.g., "log(x2)"). TRUE (default filter_terms()), extracts filters underlying raw column names (e.g., "x2"). .term logical. FALSE (default), get_variables() returns flat character vector across whole model. TRUE, returns named list mapping term label constituent variables. keep, drop character vector term labels (matched order-invariantly via match_labels()) integer vector term indices explicitly retain (keep) exclude (drop) filter_terms(). order integer vector specifying interaction orders retain filter_terms() (e.g., 1L main effects, 2L two-way interactions). require character vector variable names. terms containing least one variables retained. remove character vector variable names. terms containing variables excluded. response logical. Whether retain response variable filter_terms(). Defaults TRUE. strict logical. TRUE (default), make_signature() match_labels() require element single valid term. nomatch character string specifying handle unmatched labels match_labels(): "pass" (returns NA), "omit" (drops unmatched elements), "fail" (throws error).

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels — modelterms
text: model formula y ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + (x1 * x2), package distinguishes three structural levels: Term Labels (get_labels(x)):     individual additive components model:     c("x1", "log(x2)", "(x1 * x2)", "x1:log(x2)"). Model Variables (get_variables(x, raw = FALSE)):     distinct predictor expressions forming terms (rows "factors" matrix):     c("x1", "log(x2)", "(x1 * x2)"). Raw Variables (get_variables(x, raw = TRUE)):     underlying column names required data:     c("x1", "x2").

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels — modelterms
text: x character vector, as_terms() distinguishes vector strict term labels length-1 formula shorthand: Strict Term Labels (character(n)): every element (excluding     intercept tokens like "1" "-1") represents strictly single valid     term (e.g., c("b:", "", "(x^2)")), input order exact interaction notation     ("b:") preserved default (keep.order = TRUE). Length-1 Formula Shorthand (character(1)): x single     string containing formula operators . (e.g., ".^2", ".",     "* b + c + 1"), expanded right-hand side formula expression     (using data needed) sorted interaction order default     (keep.order = FALSE). Invalid Mixed Vectors (length(x) >= 2): x length 2     contains non-single-term expression (c("* b", "c")     c(".", "")), informative error thrown.

what: Safe Alternatives to Base R stats Functions
title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels — modelterms
text: filter_terms() serves declarative, crash-safe replacement drop.terms, delete.response, [.terms: filter_terms(x, response = FALSE) safely removes response variable     like stats::delete.response(x). filter_terms(x, drop = ...) filter_terms(x, keep = ...) subset     specific terms character label (order-invariant) numeric index without crashing     terms dropped.

title: Coerce, Inspect, Filter, and Match Model Terms and Labels — modelterms
code: # Coercion with as_terms() t1 <- as_terms(c("b:a", "a", "1")) get_labels(t1) #> [1] "b:a" "a"   has_intercept(t1) #> [1] TRUE  t2 <- as_terms(".^2", y = "Ozone", data = airquality[, 1:4]) get_labels(t2) #> [1] "Solar.R"      "Wind"         "Temp"         "Solar.R:Wind" "Solar.R:Temp" #> [6] "Wind:Temp"     # Extracting labels, variables, and response at three levels fml <- log(y) ~ x1 + log(x2) + x1:log(x2) + I(x1 * x2) get_response(fml, raw = FALSE) #> [1] "log(y)" get_response(fml, raw = TRUE) #> [1] "y" get_labels(fml) #> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" "x1:log(x2)" get_variables(fml, raw = FALSE) #> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" get_variables(fml, raw = TRUE) #> [1] "x1" "x2" get_variables(fml, raw = TRUE, each.term = TRUE) #> $x1 #> [1] "x1" #>  #> $`log(x2)` #> [1] "x2" #>  #> $`I(x1 * x2)` #> [1] "x1" "x2" #>  #> $`x1:log(x2)` #> [1] "x1" "x2" #>   # Filtering terms by order, variables, or specific term labels fml |> filter_terms(order = 1) |> get_labels() #> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" fml |> filter_terms(require = "x2", remove = "x1", raw = TRUE) |> get_labels() #> [1] "log(x2)" fml |> filter_terms(drop = "log(x2):x1", response = FALSE) #> ~1 + x1 + log(x2) + I(x1 * x2) #> attr(,"variables") #> list(x1, log(x2), I(x1 * x2)) #> attr(,"factors") #>            x1 log(x2) I(x1 * x2) #> x1          1       0          0 #> log(x2)     0       1          0 #> I(x1 * x2)  0       0          1 #> attr(,"term.labels") #> [1] "x1"         "log(x2)"    "I(x1 * x2)" #> attr(,"order") #> [1] 1 1 1 #> attr(,"intercept") #> [1] 1 #> attr(,"response") #> [1] 0 #> attr(,".Environment") #> <environment: 0x5f32d1b3d848>  # Signatures and order-invariant label matching make_signature(c("log(x2):x1", "x1 + x2")) #> [1] "log(x2):x1" NA           match_labels(c("x1", "log(x2):x1", "I(x2 * x1)"), fml, nomatch = "pass") #> [1] "x1"         "x1:log(x2)" NA
